title: Format validity and approval authority are separable, and the e-invoicing demo shows both on one screen
content:
The demo is three components in one view. Mustangproject parses an XRechnung, the KoSIT validator computes an acceptance result, and Switchboard records who accepted it, under which rule, with the prior state. Putting them side by side is the argument: format and approval are different questions and are answered by different layers.

The reason to stage it visually rather than explain it is that the two are routinely collapsed. A validator that returns "conformant" looks like an approval, and for a well-formed invoice the distinction never surfaces. It surfaces on the ambiguous case, where a human has to decide whether to accept something the validator flagged — and that decision has no home in either the parser or the validator.

Two German leads carry this demo: usegroup / Mustangproject in Frankfurt at "2 · next" and agorum Software in Ostfildern at "3 · later". The first is notable because the lead is the maintainer of one of the components the demo uses, which makes the format half of the screen theirs rather than a claim about their product.
